The nbfx Status Bar API defines the pure-JavaFX status bar contract: the FxStatusElement SPI, the registry that discovers elements from the layer, and the FxStatusBar component that lays them out.
Elements are registered with @FxStatusRegistration, which generates NbFx/Status/<id>.instance layer entries carrying the alignment and position. StatusElementRegistry reads that folder and returns the elements ordered by slot, position and id; FxStatusBar places their nodes in the left, centre and right slots.
The editor contributes a caret-position element.
The project module contributes a selected-project element.
The progress module contributes a progress element.
The ordering logic is unit-tested. The API is under development until the MVP freeze.
A JDK is required only to compile; JavaFX is provided by the runtime.
Only com.gluonhq.netbeans.nbfx.statusbar is public.
Elements are read from the configuration filesystem under NbFx/Status, not from the Lookup, so the registry can also read the placement attributes.

StatusElementRegistry.discover() reads the configuration filesystem and may run on any thread. Constructing FxStatusBar and creating element nodes must run on the JavaFX Application Thread.
The elements are discovered when the status bar is built, once per window.
FxStatusBar.dispose() releases the element resources.
No special requirements.
